ops.label: Avoid: build it all at once
Industry practice: three or four nodes, then iterate
Plan the whole pipeline up front
Build it end to end before running anything
More time spent debugging than building
An early node fails and everything downstream never runs
Worse: an early node succeeds with the wrong shape, so every node configured against it is now wrong
ops.detail: No error appears. You expected a name field, it never arrives. The result is a workflow that is not correct, which is harder to spot than a broken one.

ops.label: Start with three or four nodes: input, an AI step, somewhere to put the result
Make those run end to end with real data
Add one node, remove a connection, add another
ops.detail: The three builds in this lecture are this principle performed: each one is the previous plus a small increment, and each increment is where a class of bug shows up.

ops.title: Basic LLM Chain vs AI Agent

cells.c-chain: Asking a prompt and getting a response
cells.c-agent: Uses the LLM and tools — tools, MCP servers, other software — to complete a task

cells.c-chain: No chain of thought; will never trigger tools to get information
cells.c-agent: Chains thought, asks multiple questions, goes to multiple tools
A task that needs lookups or actions

cells.c-chain: The right node for the linear answers last week's build produced
cells.c-agent: Overkill on linear Q and A — it tries to go to multiple tools, and it does not help

cells.c-local: Identical — no change between cloud and local implementation

cells.c-cloud: Years of expertise: minimal downtime and support, workflows still execute during an outage
cells.c-local: Chances of failing are much higher than the cloud
The machine has to be on all the time — you never know when a trigger fires
The laptop's IP on the same router; it stops working the moment you leave the house
Someone pulls the building's Wi-Fi cable and the server is down

cells.c-cloud: The data sits on n8n servers
cells.c-local: The one constraint that overturns everything above — if the client says the data must not go to a cloud network, it sits only on your machine
The free trial does not apply — local is unlimited
Ollama works with n8n locally, absolutely smoothly

cells.c-cloud: A VM on GCP: you pay for the machine, not for n8n
cells.c-local: Same box, but the data and the uptime are both yours to manage
